scope: The existing opening problem chapter after the runner and before the first signup choices and home-collection explanation, in English and Spanish.
rerun: Research, bilingual copy, creative direction, implementation and independent Impeccable review repeated with the current model at the user’s request.

en.heading: What does “normal” mean for your health?
en.finding: Many lab reference ranges cover the middle 95% of results in a healthy reference group.
en.context: Your health history and earlier results also help explain what a result means for you.
en.bridge: EVA explains your blood markers in plain language and helps you follow how they change.

es.heading: ¿Qué significa «normal» para tu salud?
es.finding: Muchos rangos de referencia abarcan el 95 % central de los resultados de un grupo de personas sanas.
es.context: Tu historial de salud y tus resultados anteriores también ayudan a entender qué significa un resultado para ti.
es.bridge: EVA te explica tus marcadores en un lenguaje claro y te ayuda a seguir cómo cambian.

selected.definition: Many conventional two-sided laboratory reference intervals contain the central 95% of results from a selected healthy reference population.
selected.claim_type: Statistical definition, with no survey denominator or estimate of disease prevalence.

primary_source.citation: Ichihara et al., Clinica Chimica Acta 467 (2017), 70–82, for the IFCC Committee on Reference Intervals and Decision Limits

selected.limits: Keep ‘many’, ‘results’ and ‘healthy reference group’ visible. Clinical decision limits can be based on outcomes. The 95% definition gives no estimate of missed disease, hidden deficiencies, EVA accuracy or personal health.

alternatives.question_en: You can see your results. Can you make sense of them?
alternatives.question_es: Ya puedes ver tus resultados. ¿Puedes entenderlos?
alternatives.fact: 886 of 1,817 US adults did not recognize an elevated HbA1c in a simulated result table, 48.76%.
alternatives.limits: January 2013 online experiment, ages 40–70, about half with diabetes. Values and reference ranges were shown without high/low flags.
alternatives.decision: Accurate but narrower than EVA’s personal meaning and context proposition. The task’s methodological qualifications dominated the former mobile opening.

alternatives.question_en: Your results are back. What should you ask next?
alternatives.question_es: Ya tienes tus resultados. ¿Qué deberías preguntar ahora?
alternatives.fact: 305 of 1,412 British Columbia respondents who first received results online were unsure whether clinician follow-up was needed, 21.6%.
alternatives.decision: Useful for next-step education but less direct for introducing personal interpretation and access.

alternatives.fact: NIH MedlinePlus explains that results are combined with health history and other clinical context.
alternatives.decision: Used as supporting context alongside the selected reference-range definition.

alternatives.fact: A 2026 systematic review included 39 studies and found recurring interpretation difficulties.
alternatives.limits: No pooled prevalence figure for a headline.
alternatives.decision: Background corroboration of a need for explanation and context.
The sources reviewed provide no supported rate with defined deficiencies, denominator and independent comparator. Excluded.

source_review.rationale: The normal-range question introduces the familiar reference interval, then personal context and history. This directly supports the value of understanding results. The old percentage described recognizing an already elevated example value and required longer study-method qualifications.

copy_concepts.en: What does “normal” mean for your health?
copy_concepts.decision: Selected with the qualified reference-range definition and personal-context explanation.

copy_concepts.en: You can see your results. Can you make sense of them?
copy_concepts.es: Ya puedes ver tus resultados. ¿Puedes entenderlos?
copy_concepts.decision: Alternative backed by the narrower simulated HbA1c task.

copy_concepts.en: Your results are back. What should you ask next?
copy_concepts.es: Ya tienes tus resultados. ¿Qué deberías preguntar ahora?
copy_concepts.decision: Alternative backed by the Canadian follow-up uncertainty survey.

specialist_reviews.medical_evidence: Independently verified IFCC methods and review sources, NIH patient guidance, source contexts and alternative prevalence claims.
specialist_reviews.bilingual_marketing_copy: Selected a direct question inclusive of first-time testers, one qualified factual explanation, personal context and an explicit plain-language EVA benefit.
specialist_reviews.ux_ui: Impeccable 4.9.0 Layout and Clarify applied to EVA’s existing Hanken, analog dots, ink and warm-paper composition. The direct question leads, the inline middle-95% phrase explains the healthy reference group, a neutral dotted reference-interval strip illustrates the definition, and an 18px Hanken 600 EVA bridge leads into the free and kit choices.
specialist_reviews.implementation: A separate UX and motion specialist implemented the creative concept within the existing chapter and reused the approved free and kit entry component.
specialist_reviews.independent_typography: Impeccable Typeset and Layout review of actual native version 51. All 16 English/Spanish profiles passed at 320, 390, 768 and 1,366 CSS pixels in normal and reduced-motion modes, with 44px source and action targets, readable installed Hanken 400/600, visible focus and correct evidence-before-choice reading order. Both languages also passed actual 200% browser zoom, keyboard source/choice navigation, emulated Pixel 5 touch and JavaScript-disabled discovery/enrollment navigation.

verification.source: TypeScript, production build, English/public-route audit, bilingual parity, story sections and runner startup checks passed.
verification.live_responsive: 16 of 16 English/Spanish width and motion profiles passed. At 390 CSS pixels the chapter measured about 837 px in English and 824 px in Spanish. At 320 px it measured about 858 px and 882 px respectively, with ordinary vertical scrolling.
verification.live_keyboard_zoom: English and Spanish both passed actual 200% Chromium browser zoom. The viewport changed from 1280 CSS pixels at DPR 1 to 640 CSS pixels at DPR 2. IFCC source, localized NIH source, free-report and kit actions remained keyboard reachable without horizontal overflow.
verification.live_fallback: With JavaScript disabled, the static runner loaded visibly and native discovery, free-report and kit links navigated correctly in Spanish 320px and English desktop.
verification.live_touch: English and Spanish discovery taps and native touch drags passed in emulated Pixel 5 at 390×844 CSS pixels and DPR 2.
verification.live_regression: All 14 bilingual core landing cases passed, covering opening, native Tasso playback and controls, kit, range, Alex explanation depth, signal and trend. All six signup/plan entry flows passed with no errors, findings or mutating requests.
verification.live_http: Both locale pages returned HTTP 200 with the new heading, IFCC and NIH citations, and evidence → signup choices → home-collection order.
verification.runner_timing: The runner implementation was unchanged in this release. Its deterministic startup check passed. The accepted 2.5-second choreography is inherited from the earlier verified runner releases; this rerun did not take a new runtime timing measurement.
verification.creative_review: The creative director reviewed live English desktop at 1440px and Spanish phone at 390px and requested no corrections.

preview_limit: The managed preview startup timed out before candidate rendering. Pre-publication validation used source, type and build checks. Final rendered verification used the actual native review deployment.
